html:
The Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen was the state ruled by the Zaydi imams in northern Yemen from 1918, when the Ottomans withdrew at the end of the First World War, until the revolution of 1962.

Imam Yahya, who had fought the Ottomans for years, made it one of the most isolated countries in the world. He allowed few foreigners, few schools and almost no modern roads. He lost a short war with Saudi Arabia in 1934, which set the border, and he never accepted British Aden.

Yahya was murdered in 1948. His son Ahmad ruled harshly until 1962. Days after Ahmad's death, army officers overthrew his son, starting the North Yemen Civil War. See also the Zaydi imamate.
sum: The Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen was the state ruled by the Zaydi imams in northern Yemen from 1918, when the Ottomans withdrew at the end of the First World War, until the revolution of 1962.
